output.summary: The log holds 5,050 cases, and 73.8% follow the single most common route [[overview]]. A typical case takes 4.7 days end to end, and the slowest tenth take 10 days or more [[overview]]. Waiting costs money mainly through lost early-payment discounts of €22.0k [[rule:early-payment-discount]], and the largest share sits in the wait before Partner Approval, €13.5k [[edge:Match to Engagement → Partner Approval]].

actions.action: Review the Partner Approval queue at P. Moreau and arrange cover or redistribution so approvals do not sit for days, so that early-payment discounts are no longer missed.
actions.evidence: Cases waiting for P. Moreau's Partner Approval wait a median of 110.5 h, against 22.9 h for peers [[resource:Partner Approval@P. Moreau]]. Cases with this partner are 30.2% of the slowest tenth, against 3% among all other cases [[segment:partner=P. Moreau]]. Approved cases then wait a median of 41.4 h for the payment run, which runs about twice a week at 2.04 runs [[batch:Pay Invoice@Payment Run]]. That run wait is a schedule effect, not a person's delay.
actions.impact: Shortens the largest queue in the process. P. Moreau's queue carries €13.3k of the lost early-payment discounts [[resource:Partner Approval@P. Moreau]]. This is a share of the discount-rule loss, not an extra amount.
firstSteps: Share the queue figures with P. Moreau and ask what drives the wait: workload, absence, case mix or a lack of backup.
Name a deputy approver for routine invoices and set a service time for approvals.
Flag invoices carrying 2/10 discount terms so they are approved first.
verify: Whether P. Moreau is the only approver for certain clients. Partner and practice area Tax show identical figures in the log, so the two cannot be told apart [[segment:practice_area=Tax]].
Whether approval limits or policy allow another partner to approve these invoices.
Whether the payment-run days fit within the 10-day discount window.

actions.action: Shorten the wait for supplier credit notes by chasing requests on a fixed schedule and tracking those that run long.
actions.evidence: Waiting from Request Credit Note to Receive Credit Note takes a median of 72.3 h [[edge:Request Credit Note → Receive Credit Note]]. The excess wait there carries €4.8k of the lost discounts [[edge:Request Credit Note → Receive Credit Note]]. Cases with a credit note are 39.2% of the slowest tenth, against 6.2% among other cases [[segment:passes:Receive Credit Note=yes]]. All four handlers of the request step show a similar link to slow cases, which points to the process rather than one person [[segment:resource@Request Credit Note=A. Silva]].
actions.impact: Cuts the extra wait on credit-note cases and part of the discount loss allocated to this step, €4.8k [[edge:Request Credit Note → Receive Credit Note]]. This is not additional to the discount-rule total.
firstSteps: Set a follow-up date for each credit-note request, with a reminder to the supplier.
List open requests that have waited longer than usual and chase them now.
Group the delays by supplier to see whether a few suppliers cause most of them.
verify: Whether the wait is on the supplier side, which the team cannot control directly.
Whether invoices with a pending credit note could be paid at the discounted amount and settled later.

actions.action: Investigate and stop possible duplicate vendor payments, and add an automatic duplicate check before the payment run.
actions.evidence: The duplicate-payment rule was violated in 50 cases, or 1% of cases checked [[rule:no-duplicates]]. Its cost is €29.8k over the log period, about €54.6k a year [[rule:no-duplicates]]. That cost rests on the sample's cost setting for a duplicate payment, which counts handling plus the invoice amount.
actions.impact: Removes the largest single risk in the log, an assumed €29.8k over the period [[rule:no-duplicates]]. The figure depends on the cost setting for duplicates and on how many flagged cases are real double payments.
firstSteps: Pull the flagged invoices and check with accounts payable which were actually paid twice and whether the money was recovered.
Check which fields (vendor, invoice number, amount) the current process uses to spot a repeat.
Add a hold on invoices that match a previously paid vendor, invoice number and amount before they enter a payment run.
verify: Whether some flagged cases are legitimate partial or recurring invoices rather than true duplicates.
Whether the amounts were recovered, which would reduce the real loss.

actions.action: Enforce segregation of duties by blocking the registering clerk from approving payment on the same invoice, and check that large invoices always go through Director Approval.
actions.evidence: The rule against a registering clerk approving payment was violated in 137 cases, or 2.7% [[rule:four-eyes]]. Its compliance cost is €20.6k, based on the per-violation cost setting [[rule:four-eyes]]. The director-approval rule for large invoices was violated in 37 of the cases checked, or 5.4% [[rule:director-over-10k]].
actions.impact: Lowers audit and fraud exposure. The assumed compliance cost is €20.6k for segregation [[rule:four-eyes]], and the cost for missed Director Approvals is €5.6k [[rule:director-over-10k]]. Both rest on the per-violation cost setting.
firstSteps: List the flagged segregation cases and see who registered and approved each one.
Check whether the approval system lets a user who registered the invoice also approve its payment.
Add a system block or routing rule for the two controls.
verify: Whether small teams or absence cover explain the violations.
Whether the director-approval cases were approved outside the system or skipped.

actions.action: Find out why invoices return to Match to Engagement and remove the avoidable repeats.
actions.evidence: Match to Engagement is repeated 739 times, in 11.6% of cases [[rework:Match to Engagement]]. This costs €5.4k over the period, about €9.9k a year [[rework:Match to Engagement]]. Credit-note cases show as a large group among slow cases [[segment:passes:Request Credit Note=yes]], so some repeats may follow a credit note. That is a hypothesis to test.
actions.impact: Avoidable repeats would save part of the €9.9k yearly hands-on cost [[rework:Match to Engagement]]. The saving rests on the handling minutes per step and the hourly rate in the cost settings.
firstSteps: Sample repeated cases and note the reason for each return to matching.
Separate repeats caused by credit notes from those caused by wrong or missing engagement data.
Fix the most common cause at registration, for example with a mandatory engagement reference.
verify: Whether repeats are legitimate: partial invoices, several items in one case or re-matching after a credit note.
Whether the handling time per step in the cost settings matches real effort.
